page_1.title: Wordpress Website creator
page_1.description:
Project Overview
We are a Canadian Registered Charity operating impactful programs in Africa. We are seeking to migrate, rebuild, and upgrade our existing website using WordPress to better showcase our mission and streamline our operations.
Key Objectives

Modern Redesign: 
Create a visually compelling, mobile-responsive website.
WordPress Migration: Move existing content seamlessly to a user-friendly CMS. 

Donation Integration: 
Set up secure, Canadian tax-compliant donation tools. Impact Showcase: Build dedicated sections for field updates and success stories.

Technical Requirements
Canadian Compliance: Integration with platforms like CanadaHelps or Stripe for automatic tax receipting.

Optimized Performance: Fast loading speeds for users with low-bandwidth connections in Africa.
Multi-Currency Support: Ability to accept CAD, USD, and British Pound currencies.

Easy Admin: Intuitive backend so internal staff can update content easily.

page_1.title: Volunteer Engagement Planning Volunteer
page_1.description:
ActionDignity is seeking a Volunteer Engagement Planning Volunteer to support the planning, coordination, and execution of programs and initiatives that strengthen volunteer participation, connection, and community involvement.

The volunteer will work alongside the Membership & Volunteer Engagement team to help design meaningful volunteer experiences, support engagement activities, collect feedback, and contribute ideas that improve volunteer involvement across ActionDignity programs.

This opportunity is ideal for individuals interested in community engagement, event planning, volunteer management, program development, and nonprofit operations..

Key Responsibilities:

Program & Event Planning
Assist with planning volunteer engagement activities, workshops, networking sessions, and community-building events.
Support the development of event timelines, activity plans, and logistical checklists.
Help coordinate volunteer engagement activities from planning through execution.
Contribute creative ideas for interactive activities, games, discussions, and learning opportunities.

Volunteer Engagement Strategy Support
Assist with identifying ways to increase volunteer participation and retention.
Support the development of volunteer engagement strategies for different volunteer groups.
Help create opportunities for volunteers to build skills, connect with others, and contribute to community initiatives.
Support volunteer recognition and appreciation activities.

Community Feedback & Data Collection
Assist with developing surveys, feedback forms, and evaluation tools.
Support gathering and organizing volunteer feedback after events and programs.
Help identify trends and recommendations to improve volunteer experiences.
Administrative & Coordination Support
Assist with preparing planning documents, meeting notes, and action items.
Support volunteer communications and event reminders.
Maintain organized records related to engagement activities and outcomes.


Who Should Apply?

We welcome applications from:

Students looking to gain nonprofit experience
Community members interested in civic participation
Individuals interested in event planning and engagement
Emerging leaders interested in community development

page_1.title: Volunteer at a Prestigious Business Summit! | Closes August 1ST
page_1.description:
General Volunteers are the backbone of the Black Business Summit. This is a dynamic role where specific duties will be confirmed upon your onboarding, allowing us to match tasks to your skills, interests, and the immediate needs of the event. While ideal candidates will be located in Calgary or the broader Alberta region, we are completely open to volunteers from any location who can assist remotely in the lead-up to the event. There is the opportunity of a $150 honorarium.

MORE INFO [DUE August 1ST]: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Z63RcyPHoCfjtWCQI4xmHv4Qrv9rs0ZFCICUxq8-7BQ/edit?usp=sharing

The Black Business Summit (BBS) is a one-day event hosted by the Connecting the Dots Diversity & Inclusion Council (CDDIC), taking place on September 19, 2026 in Calgary, Alberta. Designed for Black immigrant entrepreneurs and business owners, the summit will bring together 100 attendees for keynote presentations, panel discussions, a vendor marketplace, networking, live entertainment, and refreshments.
The summit is free to attend and is being organized for the first time. It is a milestone event that reflects the collective effort of a small, dedicated team, making the Volunteer Coordinator role critical to its success.

How to Apply [DUE August 1ST]
Whether you are based in Calgary for event-day support or looking to assist us remotely from elsewhere in Alberta, if you are passionate about community-building, we’d love to hear from you.
Please express your interest by sending your resume and a cover letter to blackbusinesssummit.cddic@gmail.com.
Subject Line: BBS 2026 General Volunteer Application - Your First & Last Name
Cover Letter Requirements: Please keep your letter to a single page. Be sure to address why you are interested in this role and highlight any specific areas (such as admin, marketing, or event-day logistics) that best align with your skills.
Selected candidates will be contacted to discuss how we can best match your strengths to the summit's needs.

page_1.title: GDX Conference Volunteer
page_1.description:
IAA is hosting the Game Discovery Exhibition (GDX) Conference from October 23-25. We are looking for various volunteers including but not limited to the following:

- Planning Volunteers: Attending regularly scheduled meetings to discuss all aspects of GDX conference and exhibition planning.
- Conference Content Committees: Helping to determine what content shows up at the GDX conference, doing outreach to potential speakers/panelists, and helping to develop the bios and questions.
- Marketing Outreach: Helping to boost the signal for GDX 2025 via social media, our website, Discords, and any other push channels that exist.
- Street Team: Shouting the word about GDX amongst your own networks, across the city, and more. This could include postering, handing out handbills, etc.
- Logistics: Any general task that can help prepare for GDX. This could include putting together nametags and lanyards, getting something photocopied, or helping us to move things.
- Pre-Event Transportation: If you have a large vehicle that can help us move GDX stuff in the days before the big event, let us know!
- Front of House: Help check folks in at the conference, make sure speakers know where to go.
- Tech Support: ensure that speakers who need assistance setting up their computers etc are provided with support.
- Photos/Video Coverage: snap photos and videos throughout the day.
- Social Media: share announcements and content throughout the time leading up to the conference and during the event itself.
- Design: update graphics and make your mark on the event.

This position is for a general pool and afterwards we will reach out with specific role assignments.

PERKS:
You'll receive at least one full day of attendance at the conference free of charge, lunch is provided, a snazzy looking volunteer shirt, and access to speakers.

page_2.title: Social Media Intern (Volunteer)
page_2.description:
Full Job Description

At SilverKnots Seniors Community, we’re looking for a creative and motivated Social Media Intern who’s eager to bring ideas to life, spark conversations, and help a meaningful cause stand out in the digital space. Here, your creativity won’t be boxed in—you’ll have the freedom to experiment, learn, and grow alongside a supportive and purpose-driven team.

Join us and play a key role in shaping social strategies that drive engagement, inspire action, and build a vibrant community supporting seniors across Calgary.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us

Remote-first & flexible: Work from anywhere with a schedule that supports your work-life balance.
Make an impact: Your ideas will directly support a non-profit organization dedicated to seniors’ well-being.
Grow your career: Gain hands-on experience and build a strong portfolio in social media marketing.
Collaborative culture: Work with a passionate, visionary team that values creativity and initiative.
Purpose-driven work: Be part of a mission that puts seniors first and creates real community impact.
What You’ll Do

Create Standout Content: Develop engaging posts, stories, reels, and updates that capture attention and drive interaction.
Visual Storytelling: Source, edit, and design graphics and photos that reflect our mission and community.
Promotional Strategy: Assist in refreshing weekly content to keep messaging timely and relevant.
Profile Management: Help optimize and manage platforms like Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, WhatsApp Communities, and Google Business.
Data-Driven Insights: Track performance metrics and identify opportunities to improve engagement.
Content Planning: Support the development and maintenance of a consistent social media calendar.
What We’re Looking For

A creative, positive, and detail-oriented mindset with a passion for storytelling
1–2+ years of experience (or strong interest) in social media or digital marketing
Strong writing, editing, and communication skills in English (text, photo, and video)
Preferably a candidate familiar with Indian Heritage and Culture or other Indian languages
Familiarity with major social media platforms and basic knowledge of AI, scheduling, or analytics tools
Ability to manage multiple tasks and stay organized
Experience with short-form/vertical video (Reels, TikTok) is an asset
A willingness to learn, grow, and contribute in a team environment
Diploma or certificate (or currently pursuing) in Communications, Marketing, Business, PR, Journalism, or related field

page_2.title: Project Manager - Island Kids Cancer Association
page_2.description:
Project Management Volunteers (PMV) Sponsored Project
This is a PMV sponsored project. The Project Manager will enter into a 3-way partnership between the Client organization, the Project Manager, and PMV. This will include additional responsibilities and benefits for the Project Manager.

Our Client Organization
Island Kids Cancer Association (IKCA) is a Vancouver Island-based charity supporting children, youth, and families navigating a childhood cancer diagnosis. IKCA provides practical assistance, family connections, mental health and wellness support, and financial assistance to families across Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands.
As IKCA approaches its 10th anniversary in September 2027, the organization wishes to celebrate its impact, increase awareness of childhood cancer, strengthen community partnerships, and build sustainable support for future growth.

Project Summary
September is Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, making September 2027 a significant milestone as IKCA celebrates its 10th anniversary.
The organization is seeking an experienced Volunteer Project Manager to facilitate strategic planning workshops, guide stakeholder engagement, and help develop a comprehensive anniversary campaign strategy.

The project will be delivered in two phases.
PHASE 1 – Anniversary and Awareness Strategy Development and Campaigns Planning
The Volunteer Project Manager will work closely with IKCA leadership, staff, board members, volunteers, families, and key stakeholders to:
- Facilitate brainstorming and visioning workshops
- Explore awareness, fundraising, community engagement, and advocacy opportunities
- Evaluate options ranging from multiple smaller campaigns to one or more signature events
- Define goals, success measures, target audiences, and strategic priorities
- Develop a roadmap for activities leading up to September 2027
- Create an implementation plan and resource requirements
The outcome of Phase 1 will be a recommended anniversary strategy and approved project plan.

Required Qualifications
Minimum 5 years of project management experience
Experience facilitating strategic planning workshops and stakeholder engagement sessions
Strong communication and relationship-building skills
Experience working with nonprofit organizations is considered an asset
Experience with event planning, fundraising campaigns, or community engagement initiatives is considered an asset
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholder groups including board members, staff, volunteers, families, and community partners
Strong organizational, planning, and risk management skills.

Scope of Work
Phase 1 – Strategy Development
Facilitate strategic planning and brainstorming workshops
Lead stakeholder identification and engagement activities
Assess opportunities, risks, resource requirements, and feasibility of proposed initiatives
Develop anniversary campaign options and recommendations
Create project roadmap and implementation strategy
Establish project governance and reporting approach

Deliverables
Project Charter
Stakeholder Analysis and Engagement Plan
Facilitation of Strategic Planning Workshops
Awareness Campaign Strategy and Recommendations
Risk Register and Risk Management Plan
Project Implementation Plan and Schedule
Resource Management and Communication Plan
Status Reports for the Executive Director
Final Project Summary and Lessons Learned Report

Additional Information
We may proceed with interviewing and engaging applicants before the application deadline.
We may ask the project manager to mentor a Client team member to support raising awareness of project management techniques within the Client organization.
Applicants are welcome to apply for Phase 1 only, Phase 2 only, or both phases. Please clearly indicate your preferred phase(s) in your application.
We may choose to engage different Volunteer Project Managers for each phase depending on project needs.

page_2.title: Project Manager - Community Awareness Campaign and Annual Events
page_2.description:
Our Client Organization
The Borderline Personality Disorder Society of British Columbia (BPDBC) is a BC-based nonprofit organization supporting people living with borderline personality disorder, as well as their families, caregivers, and broader support networks.

Through education, community engagement, awareness-building, and collaboration, BPDBC seeks to reduce stigma, strengthen understanding, and improve access to meaningful support. 

Project Summary
BPDBC is seeking an experienced Volunteer Project Manager to guide the planning and delivery of a two-phase community awareness and event initiative. The project will begin with one or more facilitated brainstorming sessions to identify campaign concepts, audiences, partnerships, and event formats.

Phase 1 will move from ideation through delivery of the May 2027 event. It may also include a smaller community activity or campaign activation earlier in the project, depending on the ideas selected and available capacity. During Phase 1, the Volunteer Project Manager will also prepare a high-level plan for Phase 2.

Phase 2 will run from May/June through October 30, 2027 and will focus on detailed planning and implementation of the October awareness event or campaign.

PHASE 1 – Campaign Ideation, Planning and May Event Delivery
The Volunteer Project Manager will work closely with BPDBC leadership, staff, board members, volunteers, families, and key stakeholders to:
Facilitate one or more brainstorming and visioning sessions with the BPDBC team
Explore awareness, fundraising, community engagement, and advocacy opportunities
Generate and assess options for the May 2027 event
Evaluate proposed ideas against available time, budget, volunteer capacity, partnerships, accessibility, and risk
Define goals, success measures, target audiences, and strategic priorities
Recommend a preferred campaign and event concept for approval
Develop and maintain the detailed project plan, schedule, roles and responsibilities, communication approach, and risk register for the May event
Coordinate stakeholders, volunteers, partners, speakers, venues, suppliers, and other contributors as required
Lead regular project meetings, progress reporting, issue resolution, and readiness reviews
Support implementation and delivery of the May 2027 event
Complete a post-event review and capture lessons learned
Prepare a high-level scope, roadmap, preliminary milestones, resource assumptions, and transition recommendations for Phase 2
The outcome of Phase 1 will be a successfully delivered May 2027 event, documented lessons learned, and an approved high-level plan for the October 2027 initiative.

Required Qualifications
Minimum 5 years of project management experience
Experience facilitating strategic planning workshops and stakeholder engagement sessions
Strong communication, collaboration and relationship-building skills
Experience working with nonprofit organizations is considered an asset
Experience with event planning, fundraising campaigns, or community engagement initiatives is desired
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholder groups including board members, staff, volunteers, families, and community partners
Strong organizational, planning, problem-solving and risk management skills

Scope of Work
Phase 1 – Strategy Development and May Event Delivery
Facilitate strategic planning and brainstorming workshops
Lead stakeholder identification and engagement activities
Assess opportunities, risks, resource requirements, and feasibility of proposed initiatives
Create project roadmap and implementation strategy
Establish the project schedule, RACI/roles, meeting cadence, communication plan, and risk register
Coordinate execution and delivery of the May event and any approved smaller activation
Close Phase 1 and prepare the Phase 2 high-level roadmap and transition package

Deliverables
Project Charter
Stakeholder Analysis and Engagement Plan
Facilitation of Strategic Planning Workshops
Campaign and Event Options Assessment with Recommendation
Risk Register and Risk Management Plan
Project Implementation Plan and Schedule
Resource Management and Communication Plan
Transition Plan from Phase 1 to Phase 2
Status Reports for the President
Final Project Summary and Lessons Learned Report

Additional Information
BPDBC and PMV may begin interviewing and engaging applicants before the application deadline
Applicants may indicate interest in Phase 1 only or in both phases
The Phase 1 Volunteer Project Manager will complete delivery of the May event and prepare the high-level Phase 2 plan
Continuation into Phase 2 will be confirmed jointly by BPDBC, PMV, and the Volunteer Project Manager. BPDBC and PMV may recruit a different Volunteer Project Manager for Phase 2 depending on availability and project needs.

page_2.title: English Conversation Circle Facilitator

English Conversation Circle Facilitator Volunteers work with HMC Connections to support newcomers by leading small groups in casual English conversation practice. page_2.title: Volunteer Art Class Assistant - Sculpture | Wednesdays 10:00-11:30 AM
page_2.description:
Cool Arts Society is looking for a friendly, reliable, and compassionate volunteer to support our Sculpture class for adults living with intellectual disabilities.

This weekly class invites artists to explore the world of three-dimensional art, experimenting with a variety of materials, shapes, forms, textures, and creative construction techniques.

As a volunteer, you will assist the instructor and artists during the class, help prepare and organize materials, provide one-on-one or small-group support when needed, and encourage artists as they develop their ideas and bring their creations to life.

The class is designed to be fun, hands-on, supportive, and inclusive, giving every artist the opportunity to experiment, work at their own pace, and express their individual creativity through sculpture.

No sculpture or previous artistic experience is required. What matters most is your patience, reliability, open-mindedness, and ability to connect with and encourage others.

Commitment:
📅 Wednesdays - 10 weeks
🗓️ September 9 - November 11, 2026
🕙 10:00 AM - 11:30 AM
📍 Rotary Centre for the Arts, Kelowna

We are looking for someone who can ideally commit to the full 10-week fall season, helping our artists and volunteers build familiarity, trust, and meaningful connections throughout the program.

page_2.title: Kids' Community Kitchen Volunteers
page_2.description:
The DTES Neighbourhood House is looking for volunteers to assist with our Kids' Community Kitchen after school program on Fridays from 3-6:30pm. This is an unpaid position. 

Kids' Community Kitchen provides fun, enriching, cooking classes for up to 15 children aged 6-12. Through this program—which runs in 12-week cycles—our young participants develop a wide repertoire of cooking and kitchen-safety skills and learn about food-related topics, including nutrition, meal-planning, food-safety, and cultural diversity. The main dish and dessert recipes are chosen every week by the participants, with assistance from staff. Sessions end with a group conversation reflecting the individual children's interests, curiosities, and cultural backgrounds. The term wraps up with an exciting food related field trip. Recent examples have included Science World, and the Burnaby Christmas Village Museum. In addition to the practical skills and knowledge that children acquire through our Kids' Community Kitchen Program, participants also develop a powerful sense of competence and agency regarding their food and nutrition. Like all DTES NH programs, Kids' Community Kitchen sessions are positive, community-building events, set in a safe and nurturing space. 

VOLUNTEER DUTIES 
Volunteers duties include: guiding kids through the cooking workshop and supervising their safety and well-being; prep for and participate in art projects; after-meal clean up. 

ASSETS 
We ideally seek volunteers who have the ability to apply creative problem solving, have experience working with children and youth, and have experience with food handling and preparation. We are especially seeking someone with cooking experience and knowledge. Some other valuable assets include: 
- lived/living experience in the DTES 
- work/volunteer experience in the DTES 
- ability to speak multiple languages 

REQUIREMENTS 
We require a minimum 12-week commitment for this position. Kids' Community Kitchen volunteer applicants will undergo a 45min phone interview/screening call and a vulnerable sector check (free). The volunteer will need to come 30min early on the first day for a Kids' Community Kitchen orientation. Other requirements include: 
- understanding and support of the DTES Neighbourhood House's mission and philosophies 
- ability to work respectfully with people of diverse backgrounds and experiences 
- openness to learning from and honouring community members 
- ability to work as a team and help each other 
- reviewing our Kitchen Safety Training Materials and select parts of our Volunteer Handbook before the first shift 

APPLYING: 
If you are interested, please send fill out an application through Volunteer Impact: https://bttr.im/0lcrc

For more information, please send us an email at ed@dtesnhouse.ca. We would love you to join our team and help us prepare a meal for our community. 

ABOUT THE DTES NEIGHBOURHOOD HOUSE:   
Our mission is to provide opportunities for residents to meaningfully engage with and contribute to their community in an equitable atmosphere of sharing and learning. The secular, grassroots Downtown Eastside Neighbourhood House (DTES NH) embraces people of all ancestries, genders, ages and descriptions; annually welcoming almost 9,000 DTES residents in a community where 70% of our neighbours have low‐incomes, 700 are homeless and 5,000 are under-housed.  Those who built the DTES NH put the Right to Food at the heart of our work, as nutritional vulnerability was a theme familiar to all. Our goal around the Right to Food is to reform the nutritional impact, quality, abundance and delivery of food in the DTES in consultation with residents, community food providers, non‐food community organizations, healthcare professionals, policy makers, growers/suppliers, food/beverage industry professionals and researchers. Learn more about our organization & programs at dtesnhouse.ca  

The Downtown Eastside Neighbourhood House is situated on the unceded traditional territory of the Coast Salish Peoples, including the territories of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm, səlilwətaɬ, and Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Nations

page_3.title: Leaps in Literacy Program Volunteer - Rotary Youth Centre [Burlington]
page_3.description:
Location: 560 Guelph Line, Burlington, ON L7R 3M4
Day of Week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and/or Thursday

Commitment: 1 x night per week per program session required
Fall: September 28, 2026 - December 4, 2026
Winter: January 11, 2027 - March 12, 2027
Spring: April 5, 2027 – June 4, 2027 

Under the guidance of a Program Educator, volunteers support the delivery of the Leaps in Literacy program and help create a safe, inclusive, and encouraging learning environment where students can build literacy skills, confidence, and a love of learning.

Leaps in Literacy serves children in Grades 1–8 with diverse learning needs. Volunteers work alongside educators to support students through structured literacy activities, educational games, and individualized encouragement. Responsibilities may include assisting with student arrival and dismissal, providing movement breaks as needed, tracking student responses during lessons, and offering one-to-one support to students who require additional assistance. Comprehensive training is provided and mandatory for all volunteers.

Volunteers must be at least 16 years of age. Volunteers who are 18 years of age or older must provide a clear Vulnerable Sector Check, dated within the past 12 months. Additional volunteer opportunities may be available based on program needs and mutual interest.

Responsibilities
Arrive at least 15 minutes before the scheduled start of each session.
Support Program Educators and staff in delivering high-quality literacy programming.
Assist with student arrival and dismissal procedures and help maintain a safe, welcoming, and inclusive learning environment.
Work collaboratively with Program Educators to support students' literacy development and individual learning goals.
Assist with engaging, interactive, and multisensory literacy activities that support reading, spelling, vocabulary, fluency, and comprehension skills.
Provide one-to-one or small-group support to students who benefit from additional guidance and encouragement.
Observe and track student responses, errors, and progress during lessons as directed by Program Educators.
Encourage student confidence, perseverance, and a positive attitude toward learning.
Serve as a positive role model by demonstrating patience, empathy, respect, and inclusive behaviour.
Assist Program Educators with recording student progress and supporting ongoing program evaluation.
Complete other related duties as mutually agreed upon with program staff.

Requirements
Be at least 16 years of age.
Attend and complete mandatory volunteer training.
Volunteers 18 years of age and older must provide a clear Vulnerable Sector Check dated within the past 12 months.
Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, and a commitment to supporting children and youth.
Be comfortable working with students in Grades 1–8 with diverse learning needs.
Commit to creating a positive, respectful, and inclusive environment for all learners.
